questions.question: A good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up.
Let them pass you.
Make gestures at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will not help. They may just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is even more dangerous.

questions.question: If you are riding behind another vehicle at night, how can you tell if there are bumps on the road ahead?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Look at the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead to see if it is bouncing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, watch the vehicle ahead of you to see road conditions. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps on the road ahead.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Ready the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, pick a lane position that other drivers can see. Be ready to use the clutch and brakes quickly. Slow down as you approach. Do not change your speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind it.
Stop and wait until it starts moving again.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with lights flashing, move to a different lane to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Drink coffee.
Limit how many hours you ride each day.
Play loud music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how many hours you ride each day.
questions.explanation: On a long trip, take frequent breaks to rest. Do not ride more than six hours a day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tired faster, so dress to protect yourself from the weather.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same as normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means the motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a green signal before turning.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.

options.text: More noticeable than
Just as noticeable as
Not as noticeable as

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a larger vehicle's brake light. Other drivers may not see your brake light, especially when your taillight is on. Be aware of this.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
Avoid heavy traffic areas.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To avoid danger while riding, constantly scan the road ahead. Watch for hazards before you reach them so you can react in time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow traffic light warns that the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, keep going.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle have less traction for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is leaning.
When a motorcycle is straight up and down.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a motorcycle is leaning.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans in a turn or curve, there is less grip available for braking. You can still use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: They are less dangerous than using either one alone.
They balance each other out.
Their effects can be stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects can be stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it harder to ride safely. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do when stopping your motorcycle with a passenger?

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Fit into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. When carrying a passenger, slow down earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps when merging or crossing traffic.

questions.question: What lane position best prevents other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing in next to you. Also, riding in the center makes you more visible in a car's rearview mirror, where the driver will notice you most.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle in a parallel parking space next to a curb?

options.text: Angle the motorcycle with the rear wheel near the curb.
Angle the motorcycle with the front wheel near the curb.
Park the motorcycle on the grass away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Angle the motorcycle with the rear wheel near the curb.
questions.explanation: For parallel parking next to a curb, angle the motorcycle with the rear wheel toward the curb. Some cities require motorcycles to park parallel to the curb instead.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your whole face.
Your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes in a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for the weather.
Turning too wide in a curve.
Running off the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is motorcyclists turning too wide in a curve. Turning too wide can make you leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: Which brakes should you use when stopping?

options.text: Both brakes.
The front brake only.
The rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop. Being able to brake quickly with both brakes is important.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react quickly and maneuver if someone else makes a mistake on the road.

questions.question: What should you do when making a U-turn?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle steady.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can make the bike tip over. Use the rear brake instead to control your speed.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you in many ways. It makes you more visible to others and helps you see them. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should keep other drivers out of your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally be:

options.text: In a single line.
In pairs.
In a staggered pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered pattern.
questions.explanation: A staggered pattern is the best way for a group to stay close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. This gives you the best grip on the wet road.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a single line.
Ride in pairs.
Use a staggered pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a staggered pattern.
questions.explanation: A staggered pattern keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a road.

questions.question: When preparing to ride with a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to get on after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you. They should hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
